decision.detail: I walk to the Greyhound terminal. Third bench from the left, armrest sticks up on the right. I sit. Coat over my knees. I close my eyes. I do not go to the ballroom. I do not go to the Rialto. I do not pick up the phone. The lights over there are for someone else. My body needs to be at a specific address at a specific time in eleven hours, and the surest way to make that happen is to sleep where I already am and walk, not run, when I wake. I will drink one bad coffee at six-fifteen. I will be at the door at seven-thirty. The couch goes through the door. Not the window. That is the whole evening.
decision.intention: Remove every variable between now and 7:30 except my own legs. She does not need another call. The van does not need another call. The ballroom does not need me. The Rialto does not need me. I need to be a body at a door at a time, and the couch needs to be a thing that fits through that door. Sleep is the shortest distance between the bench and her hallway.
